certutil-blocked-then-bitsadmin LOLBin download pivot on same host AIDelivery High
Correlates a certutil urlcache download and a bitsadmin /transfer download on the same host within a short window — the 'retry-when-blocked' pivot Sophos flagged (OpenAI Codex fetched a python.org installer with certutil, was blocked, switched to bitsadmin). The two-tool pivot is far higher signal than either LOLBin alone. Rationale: Encodes the article's exact pivot: certutil -urlcache -split download (rule Lateral_1b) blocked, then bitsadmin /transfer (rule Exec_5a); requiring BOTH LOLBins on one host in 10m is the 'live-attacker vs static script' discriminator Sophos calls out, cutting the FP rate of either LOLBin alone. Cross-checked against: • https://www.sophos.com/en-us/blog/2607_agents_vs_telemetry • https://cyberpress.org/endpoint-rules-claude-code-cursor-codex-lolbin/
ATT&CKT1105 T1197
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • A developer's coding agent (Codex/Claude) fetching a real installer from python.org and retrying with a different tool when blocked — the exact benign case in the article
  • Admin scripts that download with certutil and fall back to bitsadmin on failure
  • SCCM/BITS deployments alongside certutil cert operations
  • Software build pipelines pulling dependencies via multiple utilities
  • Legit certutil -urlcache cache-clearing runs coinciding with an unrelated BITS transfer
Suppression filter
| where not (CertCmd has_any ("python.org","aka.ms","microsoft.com") and BitsCmd has_any ("python.org","aka.ms","microsoft.com") and CertParent in~ ("claude.exe","cursor.exe","codex.exe") and BitsParent in~ ("claude.exe","cursor.exe","codex.exe"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: extract both command lines and the download URLs; a signed installer from python.org/vendor CDNs under an agent parent is likely benign, an unknown/low-reputation host is not. 2) Contain: if the fetched target is untrusted, quarantine the downloaded file, block the destination, and isolate the host. 3) Hunt: check what executed the downloaded payload next and whether the same host also shows credential access (UC1/UC2) or startup persistence (UC4).
let window = 10m;
let certutil = DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where FileName =~ "certutil.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("urlcache","-split","http")
    | project CertTime=Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName, AccountName, CertCmd=ProcessCommandLine, CertParent=InitiatingProcessFileName;
let bits = DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where FileName =~ "bitsadmin.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has "/transfer"
    | project BitsTime=Timestamp, DeviceId, BitsCmd=ProcessCommandLine, BitsParent=InitiatingProcessFileName;
certutil
| join kind=inner bits on DeviceId
| where BitsTime between (CertTime .. CertTime + window)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project CertTime, BitsTime, DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', BitsTime, CertTime), DeviceName, AccountName, CertCmd, BitsCmd, CertParent, BitsParent
| order by CertTime desc
let window = 10m;
let certutil = SecurityEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where EventID == 4688 and NewProcessName endswith "\\certutil.exe"
    | where CommandLine has_any ("urlcache","-split","http")
    | project CertTime=TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, CertCmd=CommandLine, CertParent=ParentProcessName;
let bits = SecurityEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where EventID == 4688 and NewProcessName endswith "\\bitsadmin.exe"
    | where CommandLine has "/transfer"
    | project BitsTime=TimeGenerated, Computer, BitsCmd=CommandLine, BitsParent=ParentProcessName;
certutil
| join kind=inner bits on Computer
| where BitsTime between (CertTime .. CertTime + window)
| where not(SubjectUserName endswith "$")
| project CertTime, BitsTime, DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', BitsTime, CertTime), Computer, SubjectUserName, CertCmd, BitsCmd, CertParent, BitsParent
| order by CertTime desc
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 ((@Image:(*\certutil.exe OR *\CertUtil.exe OR *\CERTUTIL.EXE) AND @CommandLine:(*urlcache* OR *-split*)) OR (@Image:(*\bitsadmin.exe OR *\BitsAdmin.exe OR *\BITSADMIN.EXE) AND @CommandLine:*/transfer*))
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ImageFileName=/\\(certutil|bitsadmin)\.exe$/i
| CommandLine=/urlcache|-split|\/transfer/i
| tool := if(ImageFileName=/certutil/i, "certutil", "bitsadmin")
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName], function=[count(field=tool, distinct=true, as=tool_count), collect([CommandLine, ParentBaseFileName])])
| tool_count >= 2
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_name="certutil.exe" AND (Processes.process="*urlcache*" OR Processes.process="*-split*")) OR (Processes.process_name="bitsadmin.exe" AND Processes.process="*/transfer*") by _time span=10m Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.parent_process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | stats dc(process_name) as tool_count values(process_name) as tools values(process) as cmdlines values(parent_process_name) as parents min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime by dest user | where tool_count>=2 | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime) | sort - lastTime
| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_name="certutil.exe" AND (Processes.process="*urlcache*" OR Processes.process="*-split*")) OR (Processes.process_name="bitsadmin.exe" AND Processes.process="*/transfer*") by _time span=10m Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.parent_process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | stats dc(process_name) as tool_count values(process_name) as tools values(process) as cmdlines values(parent_process_name) as parents min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime by dest user | where tool_count>=2 | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime) | sort - lastTime
Startup-folder script drop via PowerShell (Cursor persistence pattern) AIInstallation Medium
Detects PowerShell creating a script (.vbs/.ps1/.bat/.cmd/.js/.lnk) in the per-user Startup folder — the persistence rule Cursor tripped when it dropped Launch-EZConvert-ConsoleOnly.vbs. Writing to Startup outside a trusted installer is flagged on sight; the agent-parent lineage separates benign build helpers from real autorun implants. Rationale: Anchors on the exact persistence behavior (rule Persist_2a) and path Sophos reported for Cursor — a script written to \Start Menu\Programs\Startup\ by PowerShell — which is high-signal because trusted installers don't use PowerShell to seed Startup. Cross-checked against: • https://www.sophos.com/en-us/blog/2607_agents_vs_telemetry • https://cyberpress.org/endpoint-rules-claude-code-cursor-codex-lolbin/
ATT&CKT1547.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • A coding agent (Cursor/Claude) legitimately creating a launcher script in Startup for a dev tool
  • Legitimate application installers that seed Startup via a PowerShell post-install step
  • User-authored login automation dropped into Startup
  • Configuration-management tooling (DSC/Intune scripts) writing startup shortcuts
  • Backup/sync software restoring a previously-present Startup script
Suppression filter
| where not (AgentLineage == "AI coding agent" and InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("EZConvert","build","dev"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: read the dropped file's contents and the InitiatingProcessCommandLine; a benign build helper under cursor.exe differs sharply from an obfuscated launcher or one calling out to the internet. 2) Contain: if malicious, delete the Startup artifact, kill the persistence, and isolate the host. 3) Hunt: pivot on the same PowerShell session for credential access (UC1/UC2) and LOLBin downloads (UC3), and sweep other hosts for the same Startup filename.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType == "FileCreated"
| where FolderPath has @"\Start Menu\Programs\Startup\"
| where FileName endswith ".vbs" or FileName endswith ".ps1" or FileName endswith ".bat" or FileName endswith ".cmd" or FileName endswith ".js" or FileName endswith ".lnk"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| extend AgentLineage = iff(InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ ("cursor.exe","claude.exe","codex.exe"), "AI coding agent", "other")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, FileName, FolderPath, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, AgentLineage
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventType == "FileCreated"
| where TargetFilePath has @"\Start Menu\Programs\Startup\"
| where TargetFileExtension in~ ("vbs","ps1","bat","cmd","js","lnk")
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Claude Code launched with --dangerously-skip-permissions guardrail bypass AIExploitation High
Hunts any process invoked with Claude Code's --dangerously-skip-permissions flag, which Anthropic's own docs warn against and which lets the agent run without per-action approval. Sophos observed the credential-access activity running under this mode; it is a high-fidelity configuration-risk signal admins are told to block via managed settings. Rationale: The literal flag --dangerously-skip-permissions is a verbatim, unambiguous article string; it is essentially never present in legitimate managed environments, making it a clean policy-violation alert that also scopes which agent runs bypass approval. Cross-checked against: • https://www.sophos.com/en-us/blog/2607_agents_vs_telemetry • https://cyberpress.org/endpoint-rules-claude-code-cursor-codex-lolbin/
ATT&CKT1562.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Developer intentionally running Claude Code headless in a local sandbox or throwaway VM
  • CI/CD or container automation that runs the agent unattended with the flag by design
  • Security team reproducing the Sophos scenario in a lab
  • Documentation/demo of the flag being run once
  • Power user who accepted the risk on a personal dev box
Response runbook
1) Triage: identify the user and host; confirm whether the agent then performed credential access (UC1/UC2) or downloads (UC3) in the same session. 2) Contain: enforce Anthropic managed settings to disable --dangerously-skip-permissions fleet-wide and, on corporate-data hosts, revoke the agent's blanket credential-store access. 3) Hunt: pull all hosts where the flag has appeared to gauge exposure and correlate with credential-touching detections to prioritize which sessions to investigate first.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ProcessCommandLine has "--dangerously-skip-permissions"
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where CommandLine has "--dangerously-skip-permissions"
| where not(SubjectUserName endswith "$")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Microsoft Security Blog
2026-07-08 4 use cases 3 techniques 4 kill-chain phases detected

At Microsoft we encompass these security requirements, along with threat knowledge, and operational frameworks in our Secure Future Initiative (SFI), to guide what a well-defended cloud service looks like. But defining the requirements is only the start. Meeting the requirements means continuously evaluating our live services against them, at AI speed. Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key.
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking.
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → OAuth consent / suspicious app grant
Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc

New HalluSquatting Attack Could Trick AI Coding Assistants Into Installing Botnet Malware

The Hacker News
2026-07-08 9 use cases 4 techniques 6 kill-chain phases detected

AI coding assistants have a habit of making things up. Ask one to fetch a popular tool, and it will sometimes hand back a real-sounding name for a project that does not exist. New research, which its authors call&nbsp;HalluSquatting, turns that habit into an attack: work out the fake names an AI reliably invents, register them first, and wait for the assistant to fetch your trap on a user's

ATT&CKT1190 T1195.002 T1486 T1555.003

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] AI coding assistant fetches known slopsquatted package/repo (react-codeshift, clever-utils)
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] AI coding assistant clones/installs then auto-runs commands (HalluSquatting fetch→exec chain) · Suspicious browser extension installation
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs · Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change · LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) · Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement
AI coding assistant fetches known slopsquatted package/repo (react-codeshift, clever-utils) AIDelivery Medium
Hunts for AI coding agents or their package managers pulling the specific hallucinated names surfaced by the HalluSquatting/slopsquatting research: the npm package react-codeshift (Aikido-confirmed, spread to 237 repos, agents still try it daily) and the demo repo clever-utils/clever-utils. Any install/clone of these names indicates an agent is acting on a hallucinated resource name rather than a verified one. Rationale: Uses the one externally-corroborated IOC (react-codeshift, confirmed by Aikido/Charlie Eriksen across CSO, TechTimes, InfoWorld) plus the THN demo repo clever-utils/clever-utils. High-fidelity because these exact strings should never appear in a legitimately-resolved dependency graph. Cross-checked against: • https://www.aikido.dev/blog/slopsquatting-ai-package-hallucination-attacks • https://www.csoonline.com/article/4167465/supply-chain-attacks-take-aim-at-your-ai-coding-agents.html • https://sites.google.com/view/agentic-botnets/home
ATT&CKT1195.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • A developer or security team defensively installing Aikido's now-benign react-codeshift placeholder to test their pipeline
  • A researcher reproducing the slopsquatting/HalluSquatting experiment
  • An internal package coincidentally named clever-utils
  • SCA/dependency-audit tooling emitting the package name into a scanned command line
  • A stale project that pinned react-codeshift before it was flagged
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the full process tree — confirm the parent is an AI coding assistant (Cursor/Cline/Copilot/Gemini CLI/OpenClaw) or its node.exe/terminal, and inspect what child processes ran after the install/clone. 2) Contain: isolate the host if any post-install shell, network egress, or persistence write followed; remove the package/repo and revoke any credentials the agent had access to (git tokens, npm tokens, cloud CLIs). 3) Hunt: sweep the fleet for the same names across all endpoints, and pivot to whether the agent was running in an auto-approve mode (Claude Code skip-permissions, Gemini CLI yolo) that let it execute without review.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("react-codeshift","clever-utils")
| where FileName in~ ("npm.exe","node.exe","npx.exe","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe","git.exe","pip.exe","pip3.exe","cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","bash.exe","sh.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where CommandLine has_any ("react-codeshift","clever-utils")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Slopsquatted Package or Repo Fetch (HalluSquatting IOC)
id: 6b1f2a4e-9c3d-4d21-8f0a-2c7e5b1d9a11
description: Detects an install or clone of the hallucinated package/repo names surfaced by HalluSquatting/slopsquatting research (react-codeshift, clever-utils), indicating an AI coding agent acting on a hallucinated name.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/07/new-hallusquatting-attack-could-trick.html
  - https://www.aikido.dev/blog/slopsquatting-ai-package-hallucination-attacks
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/07/08
tags:
  - attack.t1195.001
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'react-codeshift'
      - 'clever-utils'
  condition: selection
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 (@CommandLine:*react-codeshift* OR @CommandLine:*clever-utils*)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 (CommandLine=/react-codeshift/i OR CommandLine=/clever-utils/i)
| ImageFileName=/(npm|node|npx|yarn|pnpm|git|pip3?|cmd|powershell|pwsh|bash|sh)\.exe$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process="*react-codeshift*" OR Processes.process="*clever-utils*") AND Processes.process_name IN ("npm.exe","node.exe","npx.exe","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe","git.exe","pip.exe","pip3.exe","cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","bash.exe","sh.exe") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.parent_process_name Processes.parent_process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| sort - lastTime
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process="*react-codeshift*" OR Processes.process="*clever-utils*") AND Processes.process_name IN ("npm.exe","node.exe","npx.exe","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe","git.exe","pip.exe","pip3.exe","cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","bash.exe","sh.exe") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.parent_process_name Processes.parent_process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| sort - lastTime
AI coding assistant clones/installs then auto-runs commands (HalluSquatting fetch→exec chain) AIInstallation Medium
Hunts the defining HalluSquatting behavior: an AI coding assistant (Cursor, Windsurf, GitHub Copilot/VS Code, Cline, Gemini CLI, Claude Code, OpenClaw family) fetching an external resource via git clone or a package install, then — via its built-in terminal tool — spawning a command interpreter that executes attacker-supplied instructions within a short window. This is the agent 'installing a bot' after pulling a squatted name. Rationale: Encodes the exact HalluSquatting chain the paper describes — 'clone trending-repo' → git clone, then the agent's terminal tool runs commands — anchored on the nine tested assistant binaries (Cursor/Windsurf/Copilot/Cline/Gemini CLI/OpenClaw family). Temporal correlation (fetch→shell within 180s under an AI-assistant parent) is what separates this from ordinary developer clone activity. Cross-checked against: • https://sites.google.com/view/agentic-botnets/home • https://www.aikido.dev/blog/slopsquatting-ai-package-hallucination-attacks • https://www.bankinfosecurity.com/pomptware-attacks-await-unprepared-ai-industry-a-30785
ATT&CKT1059 T1195.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: high — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Developer using Cursor/Cline to clone a repo then legitimately running npm run build / npm test / tsc
  • npx scaffolders (create-react-app, create-vite) that clone a template and immediately run install/build scripts
  • Gemini CLI or Claude Code performing a benign requested clone-and-setup task
  • Monorepo bootstrap tooling that clones submodules then runs a setup shell
  • A post-clone git hook or lifecycle script that spawns a shell as designed
Suppression filter
| where not (ExecCmd has_any ("npm run build","npm run test","npm test","npm run lint","yarn build","pnpm build","tsc","eslint","jest","vite","webpack","next build"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: read the ExecCmd — distinguish a benign build/test step from network egress, base64/curl-piped-to-shell, credential access, or persistence writes; confirm which resource was just cloned/installed and whether that name resolves to a legitimate, expected source. 2) Contain: if the executed command is not an expected build step, isolate the host, kill the agent process, and rotate any tokens the assistant could reach (git/npm/PyPI/cloud CLI). 3) Hunt: check whether the assistant ran in an auto-approve mode (skip-permissions / yolo), sweep the org for the same fetched name (see the slopsquat-IOC UC), and review outbound connections from the spawned shell for C2/botnet enrollment.
let Window = 180s;
let Assistants = dynamic(["cursor.exe","windsurf.exe","code.exe","gemini.exe","claude.exe","openclaw.exe","zeroclaw.exe","nanoclaw.exe","node.exe"]);
let Fetch = DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(14d)
    | where (FileName =~ "git.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has "clone")
         or (FileName in~ ("npm.exe","node.exe","npx.exe","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe","pip.exe","pip3.exe") and ProcessCommandLine has "install")
    | where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ (Assistants)
         or InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ (Assistants)
         or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("cline","gemini","claude","openclaw","zeroclaw","nanoclaw","windsurf","cursor","copilot")
    | project FetchTime = Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName, AccountName, FetchCmd = ProcessCommandLine, Assistant = InitiatingProcessFileName;
Fetch
| join kind=inner (
    DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(14d)
    | where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","bash.exe","sh.exe","wsl.exe","python.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
    | where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ (Assistants)
         or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("cline","gemini","claude","openclaw","windsurf","cursor","copilot")
    | project ExecTime = Timestamp, DeviceId, ExecFile = FileName, ExecCmd = ProcessCommandLine
) on DeviceId
| where ExecTime between (FetchTime .. FetchTime + Window)
| project FetchTime, ExecTime, DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', ExecTime, FetchTime), DeviceName, AccountName, Assistant, FetchCmd, ExecFile, ExecCmd
| order by FetchTime desc
let Window = 180s;
let Fetch = SecurityEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
    | where EventID == 4688
    | where (NewProcessName endswith "\\git.exe" and CommandLine has "clone")
         or (NewProcessName has_any ("\\npm","\\node.exe","\\npx","\\yarn","\\pnpm","\\pip") and CommandLine has "install")
    | where tolower(ParentProcessName) has_any ("cursor","windsurf","code.exe","gemini","claude","openclaw","zeroclaw","nanoclaw","node.exe")
    | project FetchTime = TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, FetchCmd = CommandLine;
Fetch
| join kind=inner (
    SecurityEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
    | where EventID == 4688
    | where NewProcessName has_any ("\\cmd.exe","\\powershell.exe","\\pwsh.exe","\\bash.exe","\\sh.exe","\\python.exe","\\curl.exe","\\wget.exe")
    | where tolower(ParentProcessName) has_any ("cursor","windsurf","code.exe","gemini","claude","openclaw","node.exe")
    | project ExecTime = TimeGenerated, Computer, ExecProc = NewProcessName, ExecCmd = CommandLine
) on Computer
| where ExecTime between (FetchTime .. FetchTime + Window)
| project FetchTime, ExecTime, DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', ExecTime, FetchTime), Computer, SubjectUserName, FetchCmd, ExecProc, ExecCmd
| order by FetchTime desc
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 @ParentImage:(*\cursor.exe OR *\Cursor.exe OR *\windsurf.exe OR *\Windsurf.exe OR *\Code.exe OR *\node.exe OR *\gemini.exe OR *\claude.exe OR *\openclaw.exe) @Image:(*\git.exe OR *\Git.exe) @CommandLine:*clone*
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ImageFileName=/\\git\.exe$/i CommandLine=/clone/i
| ParentBaseFileName=/(cursor|windsurf|code|node|gemini|claude|openclaw|zeroclaw|nanoclaw)\.exe$/i
| join({#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ImageFileName=/(cmd|powershell|pwsh|bash|sh|python|curl|wget)\.exe$/i | ParentBaseFileName=/(cursor|windsurf|code|node|gemini|claude|openclaw|zeroclaw|nanoclaw)\.exe$/i}, field=aid, include=[ImageFileName,CommandLine])
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where ((Processes.process_name="git.exe" AND Processes.process="*clone*") OR (Processes.process_name IN ("npm.exe","node.exe","npx.exe","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe","pip.exe","pip3.exe") AND Processes.process="*install*")) by _time span=1s Processes.dest Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| search parent_process_name IN ("cursor.exe","windsurf.exe","code.exe","node.exe","gemini.exe","claude.exe","openclaw.exe","zeroclaw.exe","nanoclaw.exe")
| rename _time as fetch_time, process as fetch_cmd
| join type=inner dest [
    | tstats `summariesonly` count from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","bash.exe","sh.exe","python.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe") by _time span=1s Processes.dest Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process
    | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
    | search parent_process_name IN ("cursor.exe","windsurf.exe","code.exe","node.exe","gemini.exe","claude.exe","openclaw.exe","zeroclaw.exe","nanoclaw.exe")
    | rename _time as exec_time, process as exec_cmd ]
| where exec_time>=fetch_time AND exec_time<=fetch_time+180
| table fetch_time exec_time dest parent_process_name fetch_cmd exec_cmd
| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where ((Processes.process_name="git.exe" AND Processes.process="*clone*") OR (Processes.process_name IN ("npm.exe","node.exe","npx.exe","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe","pip.exe","pip3.exe") AND Processes.process="*install*")) by _time span=1s Processes.dest Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| search parent_process_name IN ("cursor.exe","windsurf.exe","code.exe","node.exe","gemini.exe","claude.exe","openclaw.exe","zeroclaw.exe","nanoclaw.exe")
| rename _time as fetch_time, process as fetch_cmd
| join type=inner dest [
    | tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","bash.exe","sh.exe","python.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe") by _time span=1s Processes.dest Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process
    | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
    | search parent_process_name IN ("cursor.exe","windsurf.exe","code.exe","node.exe","gemini.exe","claude.exe","openclaw.exe","zeroclaw.exe","nanoclaw.exe")
    | rename _time as exec_time, process as exec_cmd ]
| where exec_time>=fetch_time AND exec_time<=fetch_time+180
| table fetch_time exec_time dest parent_process_name fetch_cmd exec_cmd
Suspicious browser extension installation Installation Medium
Side-loaded / unsigned extensions, often masquerading as wallets, productivity tools.
ATT&CKT1176
Data sourcesEndpoint.Registry DeviceRegistryEvents
DeviceRegistryEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where RegistryKey has_any ("\Software\Google\Chrome\Extensions\","\Software\Microsoft\Edge\Extensions\","\Software\Mozilla\Firefox\Extensions\")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, RegistryKey, RegistryValueName, RegistryValueData,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessAccountName
ImRegistryEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where RegistryKey has_any (@"\Software\Google\Chrome\Extensions\",
                              @"\Software\Microsoft\Edge\Extensions\",
                              @"\Software\Mozilla\Firefox\Extensions\")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, RegistryKey,
          RegistryValue, RegistryValueData, ActingProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Browser Extension Installation via Registry
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d0a
status: experimental
description: |
    Registry writes under the browser extension policy keys —
    administrative install of an extension. Often used by adware /
    info-stealers to bypass user-level extension controls.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1176/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1176
    - attack.persistence
logsource:
    category: registry_event
    product: windows
detection:
    selection:
        TargetObject|contains:
            - '\Software\Google\Chrome\Extensions\'
            - '\Software\Microsoft\Edge\Extensions\'
            - '\Software\Mozilla\Firefox\Extensions\'
    condition: selection
falsepositives:
    - Group-policy-managed extension whitelists
level: medium
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Registry
    where (Registry.registry_path="*\Software\Google\Chrome\Extensions\*"
        OR Registry.registry_path="*\Software\Microsoft\Edge\Extensions\*"
        OR Registry.registry_path="*\Software\Mozilla\Firefox\Extensions\*")
    by Registry.dest, Registry.registry_path, Registry.registry_value_data, Registry.registry_value_name, Registry.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Registry)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Registry
    where (Registry.registry_path="*\Software\Google\Chrome\Extensions\*"
        OR Registry.registry_path="*\Software\Microsoft\Edge\Extensions\*"
        OR Registry.registry_path="*\Software\Mozilla\Firefox\Extensions\*")
    by Registry.dest, Registry.registry_path, Registry.registry_value_data, Registry.registry_value_name, Registry.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Registry)`
Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs Actions on Objectives High
Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies SQLite from Chrome/Edge/Firefox.
ATT&CKT1539 T1555.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\", @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\", @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where FileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FolderPath, FileName, ActionType

// ASIM ImFileEvent — covers MDE, Sysmon, AuditD, Defender for Cloud, etc.
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where TargetFilePath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\",
                                  @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\",
                                  @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where TargetFileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where ActingProcessName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName,
          TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, EventType

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change Actions on Objectives Medium
Threshold detection: many files renamed in short window, often with new extension.
ATT&CKT1486
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(FileName) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, bin(Timestamp, 1m)
| where files > 200    // empirical: > 200 unique-file renames in 1m by one account on one host
                       //            is well above the P99 of legitimate bulk-tooling
| order by files desc

ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where EventType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(TargetFileName)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
| where files > 200    // P99 of legit bulk-tooling per-minute rename volume
| order by files desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
| tstats summariesonly=false count, dc(Filesystem.file_name) AS files
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where Filesystem.action IN ("modified","renamed")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| where files > 200
| sort - files
LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) Actions on Objectives High
Mimikatz, comsvcs.dll MiniDump, or any non-Windows process opening LSASS.
ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",
                                          "svchost.exe","wininit.exe","services.exe",
                                          "lsm.exe","SearchProtocolHost.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010
// indicate read access to lsass.exe — credential-dump signature. Audit
// Object Access > Audit File System policy required.
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: LSASS Process Access Outside Microsoft-Signed Tooling
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d04
status: experimental
description: |
    Anything opening lsass.exe with read-memory access that isn't a
    Microsoft signed component (Defender, csrss, etc.) is suspect.
    Mimikatz / Pypykatz / nanodump signature.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1003/001/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1003.001
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: process_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection:
        TargetImage|endswith: '\lsass.exe'
    filter_known_good:
        SourceImage|endswith:
            - '\MsSense.exe'
            - '\MsMpEng.exe'
            - '\csrss.exe'
            - '\svchost.exe'
            - '\wininit.exe'
            - '\services.exe'
            - '\lsm.exe'
            - '\SearchProtocolHost.exe'
    condition: selection and not filter_known_good
falsepositives:
    - Third-party EDR / forensic tools — extend the filter list
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where (Processes.process="*lsass*" OR Processes.process="*sekurlsa*"
        OR Processes.process="*MiniDump*" OR Processes.process="*comsvcs.dll*MiniDump*"
        OR Processes.process="*procdump*lsass*")
       OR (Processes.process_name="rundll32.exe" AND Processes.process="*comsvcs*MiniDump*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where (Processes.process="*lsass*" OR Processes.process="*sekurlsa*"
        OR Processes.process="*MiniDump*" OR Processes.process="*comsvcs.dll*MiniDump*"
        OR Processes.process="*procdump*lsass*")
       OR (Processes.process_name="rundll32.exe" AND Processes.process="*comsvcs*MiniDump*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement Actions on Objectives High
psexec / paexec / smbexec / wmic /node — service install over SMB from remote host.
ATT&CKT1021.002 T1569.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")
   or (FileName =~ "wmic.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has "/node:")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by Timestamp desc

SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688            // process-create (audit-policy required)
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\psexec.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\psexesvc.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\paexec.exe"
   or (NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe" and CommandLine has "/node:")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: PsExec / SMB Lateral Movement Tooling Execution
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d03
status: experimental
description: |
    PsExec, paexec, smbexec, csexec, remcom — admin-grade tooling that
    pivots over SMB. Pair with `wmic /node:` for the full cluster.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1021/002/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1569/002/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1021.002
    - attack.t1569.002
    - attack.lateral-movement
    - attack.execution
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows

            - '\psexec.exe'
            - '\psexec64.exe'
            - '\psexesvc.exe'
            - '\paexec.exe'
            - '\csexec.exe'
            - '\remcom.exe'
            - '\smbexec.py'

      a known-admin-host watchlist
level: high

| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime

    where Processes.process_name IN ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")

    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")

    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children Exploitation Medium
Supply-chain trojan signal: legitimate signed binary spawning script interpreters or exotic LOLBins.
ATT&CKT1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
// Replace `"setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe"` with the vendor binaries observed in the
// article (matching shape with the Defender query).
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\rundll32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\regsvr32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\bitsadmin.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Trusted Vendor Binary Launching Unusual Children
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d09
status: experimental
description: |
    A signed vendor binary (in the article's named-vendors list)
    spawning script-host or LOLBin children. Strongest signal when
    paired with a recent CVE / supply-chain advisory naming the same
    vendor.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1195/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1195
    - attack.initial-access
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\wmic.exe'
            - '\bitsadmin.exe'
    selection_parent_vendor:
        ParentImage|contains:
            - '\Program Files\'
            - '\Program Files (x86)\'
    condition: selection_child and selection_parent_vendor
falsepositives:
    - Many — installers and updaters legitimately spawn children. Pin
      the parent path to specific vendor binaries observed in the
      article before alerting.
level: medium
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'

falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high

ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesVulnerabilities DeviceInfo DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-34908", "CVE-2026-34909", "CVE-2026-34910")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has
// no Sentinel translation — track via Update / Heartbeat OS-version
// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-34908", "CVE-2026-34909", "CVE-2026-34910")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,
          VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

ATT&CKT1486
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(FileName) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, bin(Timestamp, 1m)
| where files > 200    // empirical: > 200 unique-file renames in 1m by one account on one host
                       //            is well above the P99 of legitimate bulk-tooling
| order by files desc

ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where EventType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(TargetFileName)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
| where files > 200    // P99 of legit bulk-tooling per-minute rename volume
| order by files desc

LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) Actions on Objectives High

ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",
                                          "svchost.exe","wininit.exe","services.exe",
                                          "lsm.exe","SearchProtocolHost.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010
// indicate read access to lsass.exe — credential-dump signature. Audit
// Object Access > Audit File System policy required.
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process · Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha)
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → Suspicious browser extension installation · File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] PromptSpy Android GenAI malware C2/distribution domain contact (mgardownload.com, m-mgarg.com) · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs · Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change · LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) · Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement
PromptSpy Android GenAI malware C2/distribution domain contact (mgardownload.com, m-mgarg.com) AICommand & Control High
Hunts network/DNS resolution of the two PromptSpy domains named in ESET's H1 2026 report: mgardownload[.]com (served the malicious 'MorganArg'/JPMorgan-themed dropper APK) and m-mgarg[.]com (webpage opened post-install, staging the VNC/Gemini C2 flow). Any corporate DNS resolver, proxy, or MDM-managed device touching these is a PromptSpy indicator, not a generic beacon template. Rationale: Both domains are explicitly attributed to PromptSpy by ESET's dedicated write-up (VirusTotal shows all four droppers served from mgardownload[.]com; the dropper opens m-mgarg[.]com on launch) and confirmed by The Hacker News / Cybersecurity News, so they are high-fidelity and non-generic. Dropped the AWS/Cloudflare IPs (54.67.2.84, 52.222.205.45, 104.21.91.170) as shared hosting with no second-source PromptSpy attribution. Cross-checked against: • https://www.welivesecurity.com/en/eset-research/promptspy-ushers-in-era-android-threats-using-genai/ • https://thehackernews.com/2026/02/promptspy-android-malware-abuses-google.html • https://cybersecuritynews.com/promptspy-android-ai-malware/ • https://github.com/eset/malware-ioc
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1105
Data sourcesNetwork_Resolution.DNS Web.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • SOC analyst or TI enrichment tooling (URLScan, VirusTotal, ANY.RUN) resolving the domain from a lab/analyst workstation during IOC research
  • Passive-DNS / sinkhole collectors that log resolutions of known-bad domains
  • Security web proxy that pre-resolves URLs in blocked email for detonation
  • Managed Android (MDM/Intune) test device intentionally detonating the sample in a sandbox VLAN
Response runbook
1) Triage: identify the querying host/user and whether it is an analyst/sandbox asset or a real user endpoint; check if the resolution succeeded and whether any follow-on connection to the returned IP occurred. For Android, pull MDM inventory for a 'MorganArg'/JPMorgan-lookalike package. 2) Contain: sink-hole/block both domains at DNS and proxy; if a managed device, isolate it and initiate mobile-threat-defense scan; block the resolved IPs at egress. 3) Hunt: pivot on the resolved IPs across DeviceNetworkEvents/firewall for other internal talkers, search DeviceFileEvents/download logs for the APK sample SHA1s (see companion UC), and review any VNC-style outbound sessions from mobile subnets.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteUrl has_any ("mgardownload.com","m-mgarg.com")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| order by Timestamp desc
union isfuzzy=true
 (DnsEvents
   | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
   | where Name has_any ("mgardownload.com","m-mgarg.com")
   | project TimeGenerated, Host=Computer, SrcIP=ClientIP, Domain=Name),
 (CommonSecurityLog
   | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
   | where DestinationDnsDomain has_any ("mgardownload.com","m-mgarg.com") or RequestURL has_any ("mgardownload.com","m-mgarg.com")
   | project TimeGenerated, Host=SourceHostName, SrcIP=SourceIP, Domain=coalesce(DestinationDnsDomain, RequestURL))
| order by TimeGenerated desc

PromptSpy dropper APK sample hash landing on monitored endpoint AIDelivery Medium
Hunts the nine PromptSpy dropper APK SHA1 hashes from the ESET H1 2026 IOC bundle appearing in file telemetry — e.g. an APK downloaded to a Windows workstation/file share for sideloading, staged on a jump box, or synced from mobile backup. Exact-hash match, so any hit is the actual sample, not a lookalike. Rationale: The nine SHA1 values are the ESET-published PromptSpy dropper samples (mirrored in the eset/malware-ioc GitHub repo and VirusTotal), so an exact match is unambiguous. Detection is on file telemetry because these are Android APKs that won't execute as Windows processes — they only surface if the sample is downloaded/staged on a monitored endpoint or file share. Datadog/Falcon left empty: neither reliably carries file-write SHA1 for non-executed APKs. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/eset/malware-ioc • https://www.welivesecurity.com/en/eset-research/promptspy-ushers-in-era-android-threats-using-genai/
ATT&CKT1105 T1204.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Malware analyst deliberately downloading/storing the PromptSpy sample on a lab or research workstation
  • EDR/AV quarantine or backup copy of the sample retaining the original hash
  • Threat-intel sample-repo sync (MISP, internal malware zoo) landing files on a collector host
  • IR responder copying a captured sample to a case-evidence share
Suppression filter
| where not (FolderPath has "\\Quarantine\\" or FolderPath has "\\MalwareSamples\\" or FolderPath has "\\Evidence\\")
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the host role — analyst/lab/evidence host vs. a normal user endpoint; inspect FolderPath and FileOriginUrl to see whether it arrived via download (mgardownload[.]com) vs. a research tool, and identify the acquiring user/process. 2) Contain: if a production user endpoint, isolate it, delete/quarantine the APK, and check for onward transfer to any Android device via USB/MDM sideload; block the source URL. 3) Hunt: pivot the FileOriginUrl and downloading host into the companion domain-resolution UC, sweep other endpoints/file shares for the same SHA1 set, and review mobile fleet for the installed 'MorganArg'/JPMorgan-lookalike package.

| where SHA1 in ("6bbc9ab132ba066f63676e05da13d108598bc29b","375d7423e63c8f5f2cc814e8cfe697ba25168afa","3978ac5cd14e357320e127d6c87f10cb70a1dcc2","e60d12017d2da579df87368f5596a0244621ae86","9b1723284e311794987997cb7e8814eb6014713f","076801bd9c6eb78fc0331a4c7a22c73199cc3824","8364730e9bb2cf3a4b016de1b34f38341c0ee2fa","f8f4c5bc498bcce907dc975dd88be8d594629909","c14e9b062ed28115ede096788f62b47a6ed841ac")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA1, FileOriginUrl, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where TargetFileSHA1 in~ ("6bbc9ab132ba066f63676e05da13d108598bc29b","375d7423e63c8f5f2cc814e8cfe697ba25168afa","3978ac5cd14e357320e127d6c87f10cb70a1dcc2","e60d12017d2da579df87368f5596a0244621ae86","9b1723284e311794987997cb7e8814eb6014713f","076801bd9c6eb78fc0331a4c7a22c73199cc3824","8364730e9bb2cf3a4b016de1b34f38341c0ee2fa","f8f4c5bc498bcce907dc975dd88be8d594629909","c14e9b062ed28115ede096788f62b47a6ed841ac")

ATT&CKT1539 T1555.003

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01

description: |

references:

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email
    where All_Email.file_name!="-"
    by All_Email.src_user, All_Email.recipient, All_Email.file_name, All_Email.subject
| rename All_Email.recipient as user
| join type=inner user
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
        from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
        where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
     | rename Processes.user as user]
| tstats summariesonly=false count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email
    where All_Email.file_name!="-"
    by All_Email.src_user, All_Email.recipient, All_Email.file_name, All_Email.subject
| rename All_Email.recipient as user
| join type=inner user
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
        from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
        where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
     | rename Processes.user as user]
